author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Boston and its Public Health Commission are awarding $3.3 million to community health centers as the providers prepare for expected changes in insurance coverage and continued staffing pressure. The money comes from the city’s final year of American Rescue Plan Act funding.

Ten centers will receive $300,000 apiece for existing staff, insurance-enrollment assistance and care programs. A further $300,000 will go to the Massachusetts League of Community Health Centers to support longer-term financial stability, according to the city’s September 10 announcement.

MassHealth projects that new federal work and education requirements beginning in January 2027 could affect around 40,000 Boston residents. City figures place about 40% of that group in Dorchester and Roxbury, with another 20% in Hyde Park, the South End and Mattapan.

The selected providers include NeighborHealth, The Dimock Center, DotHouse Health, Codman Square Health Center and Boston Health Care for the Homeless Program. Community health centers treat patients regardless of insurance status, so the city expects them to absorb more demand if residents lose coverage. The award is one-time funding, separate from Boston’s annual support and other grants.
dek: Ten centers will receive $300,000 each, while a statewide league gets another $300,000 for financial-stability work.
headline: Boston awards $3.3 million to community health centers
